paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Judah was outnumbered two to one, 800,000 against 400,000, and then Jeroboam's ambush closed in behind them. On paper, that's not a good day. But the passage says the men of Judah "prevailed because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers" (2 Chronicles 13:18).

Notice what Judah did when the walls closed in. They "cried out to the LORD" (2 Chronicles 13:14). That's the whole move, baker. When you're stuck with trouble in front AND behind, the first thing to do is look up. And look at who gets the credit: "God routed Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah" (2 Chronicles 13:15).

Abijah's speech matters too, because it shows what relying on the LORD looks like. Judah kept showing up for what God asked, morning and evening, while the other side had "forsaken Him" (2 Chronicles 13:11). So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. Big numbers don't decide the day, and your own strength doesn't either. The God who hears a cry in the middle of a squeeze is the One to lean on, and I'd stake my whole gold base on that.
